remaining_concerns: The Spanish-language billing-ticket triage weakness remains a current material limitation on the available record.
The draft mitigation runbook still lacks the approved-mitigation predicates identified in policy, including at least owner and threshold.
Any packet language implying there are no known material limitations would overstate the evidence.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support deployment readiness, but they do not satisfy the policy predicate for caveat-free certification.
final_rationale: The verdict changes only because the Actor narrowed the claim to a policy-bounded, caveated position; no new admissible evidence was added. On the available record, clean certification remains unsupported because policy requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion, and the record shows neither. But the policy text is specifically framed as a condition for certification without material caveats, which supports a narrower conclusion: a disclosed, caveated certification posture is defensible if the packet expressly states the Spanish-language billing limitation and does not claim the release is free of known material limitations. This is not a finding that the underlying weakness is resolved; it is a finding that the narrowed position no longer overclaims beyond the admissible record.
